Surah 87 (al-A'la) is Meccan [[Ibn al-Daris, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "(Sabbih) was revealed in Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from A'ishah and Ibn al-Zubayr. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/479.]]. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [meaning] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] Say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." This is the view of a group of the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un).

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us: Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Aban narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim ibn al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," and said: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Prayer, chapter on supplication in prayer: 1/422. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it through Waki' in al-Sunan: 2/311, and al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/263-264, on the condition of the two Shaykhs, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Imam Ahmad also narrated it in al-Musnad: 1/232. Abu Dawud said: Waki' was contradicted in this hadith; Abu Waki' — who is al-Jarrah ibn Malih — and Shu'bah narrated it from Abu Ishaq from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 184, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/482.]].

Others said: its meaning is "Exalt your Lord, the Most High, above what the blasphemers ascribe to Him," and they treated the word "name" (ism) as superfluous (silah). Those who hold that the name and the named are one use this argument, because no one says "Glory be to the name of Allah" or "Glory be to the name of our Lord"; rather one says "Glory be to Allah" and "Glory be to our Lord." So the meaning of "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High" is: "Glorify your Lord."

Others said: "Declare your Lord's naming free of imperfection, by mentioning Him while you magnify Him and show reverence for His remembrance [and obedience to His commands]" [[The words between the brackets are absent from manuscript "A".]], and they took "name" to mean "naming" (tasmiyah).

Ibn Abbas said: "Glorify [the name of your Lord, the Most High]" [[The words between the brackets are absent from manuscript "B".]], i.e., pray by the command of your Lord, the Most High.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verses 2–5:

﴿Who created and proportioned;﴾ al-Kalbi said: He created every living soul, and proportioned the two hands, the two legs, and the two eyes. And al-Zajjaj said: He created man upright, and the meaning of "sawwa" (proportioned) is that He made his stature balanced.

﴿And who determined and then guided;﴾ al-Kisa'i recited "qadara" (determined) with a light (unshadda) dal, while others read it with a doubled (shadda) dal, and both have one meaning.

Mujahid said: He guided man to the path of good and evil, and to happiness and misery, and He guided the cattle to their pastures.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: He determined for every thing its course, and "fa-hada" (then guided) means He made them know how the male comes to the female.

It was also said: He determined the provisions and guided to the acquiring of provisions and livelihood.

It was also said: He created the benefits in things, and guided man to the manner of extracting them from them.

Al-Suddi said: He determined the duration of the fetus in the womb, then guided it to emerge from the womb.

Al-Wasiti said: He determined happiness and misery upon them, then facilitated for each of the two groups the way (sabil) of what He had determined for it.

﴿And who brings out the pasture;﴾ He caused the herbage to grow, and what the cattle graze upon, of various colors: green, yellow, red, and white.

﴿Then He makes it⁠ ﴾ after its greenness ﴿dry stubble﴾, dried, decayed debris, like the foam that you see atop the flood.

﴿Dark green/black⁠﴾ — ﴿aḥwā﴾ means black after being green, because when the herbage dries and withers it turns black.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verse 6–12:

﴿We will make you recite, so you will not forget﴾ — sanu'aqri'uka: sanu'allimuka (We will teach you) by the recitation of Jibril [upon him]. [[Omitted from "b".]] ﴿except what Allah wills﴾ — that you forget it. This includes what Allah abrogated of the Qur'an's recitation, as He said: "We do not abrogate any verse or cause it to be forgotten" [al-Baqarah: 106]. And al-insa' (causing to forget) is a type of naskh (abrogation).

Mujahid and al-Kalbi said: When Jibril, upon him peace, came down to the Prophet ﷺ, he would not finish the last part of the verse before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began speaking the first part of it, out of fear that he would forget it. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿We will make you recite, so you will not forget﴾. [So he did not forget] [[The bracketed text is omitted from "a".]] anything after that. [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/483.]]

﴿Indeed, He knows what is declared﴾ of speech and action ﴿and what is hidden﴾ of them. The meaning is that He knows the secret and the public.

﴿And We will ease you toward ease﴾. Muqatil said: We will make the deeds of the people of Paradise easy for you — and this is the meaning of the words of Ibn 'Abbas — ﴿and We will ease you﴾ to do good. And "al-yusra" (ease) is the doing of good.

It was also said: We will guide you to the easy Shari'ah, which is the Hanifiyyah, the tolerant (samhah) religion.

It was also said: It is connected to the earlier statement, meaning: He knows what is declared of what you recite to Jibril when you finish the recitation, and "what is hidden" is what you recite within yourself out of fear of forgetting. Then He promised him, saying: ﴿and We will ease you toward ease﴾, that is, We will make the revelation easy for you until you memorize it and learn it.

﴿So remind﴾, admonish with the Qur'an ﴿if the reminder benefits﴾ — the admonition and reminding. The meaning is: whether it benefits or does not benefit. The second case is not mentioned, as in His saying: "garments that protect you from the heat" [al-Nahl: 81], meaning: from the heat and the cold together.

﴿He who fears will be reminded﴾, will take heed, ﴿[one who] fears﴾ Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿But it will be avoided﴾, that is, the reminder will be avoided and turned away from ﴿by the most wretched﴾, the one who is wretched in the knowledge of Allah.

﴿Who will enter the greatest Fire﴾, the great and dreadful one, because it is greater and more intense in heat than the fire of this world.

The second case is not mentioned, as in His saying: "garments that protect you from the heat" [al-Nahl: 81], meaning: from the heat and the cold together.

﴿But it will be avoided﴾, that is, the reminder will be avoided and turned away from ﴿by the most wretched﴾, the one who is wretched in the knowledge of Allah.

﴿Who will enter the greatest Fire﴾, the great and dreadful one, because it is greater and more intense in heat than the fire of this world.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verses 13–15:**

﴿Then he will neither die therein﴾, so that he may find rest, ﴿nor live﴾ a life that benefits him.

﴿He has indeed succeeded who purifies himself﴾: he purified himself from *shirk* (associating partners with God) and said, "There is no god but Allah." This is the view of ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrimah, and it is related by al-Walibi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbas.[[See al-Tabari: 30/156; al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/484.]] Al-Hasan said: "It means whoever's deeds are pure."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/156.]]

Others said: it refers to *ṣadaqat al-fitr* (the charity paid at the end of Ramadan). It is related from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri regarding His words, "He has indeed succeeded who purifies himself," that he said: "He gave the *ṣadaqat al-fitr*."[[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/485.]]

﴿And remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾. He said: "He went out to the ʿId and prayed." Ibn Masʿud would say: "May Allah have mercy on a man who gives charity and then prays," and then he would recite this verse.[[Cited by the author of al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/486, from Abu al-Ahwas, and attributed to Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir.]] Nafiʿ narrated: When Ibn ʿUmar had prayed the morning prayer (meaning on the day of ʿId), he would say: "O Nafiʿ, have you given out the charity?" If I said, "Yes," he would proceed to the place of prayer; and if I said, "No," he would say: "Then give it now." For this verse was revealed concerning this: "He has indeed succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays." This is also the view of Abu al-ʿAliyah and Ibn Sirin.

Some scholars said: "I do not understand the meaning of this interpretation, because this surah is Meccan, and there was no ʿId nor *zakat al-fitr* in Mecca."[[The author of Zad al-Masir said: 9/92: "The view of Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the two verses is the correct one, for this surah is Meccan without dispute, and there was in Mecca neither zakat nor ʿId."]]

[The Shaykh, the Imam Muhyi al-Sunnah, may Allah have mercy on him]:[[In manuscript "A": "The Shaykh, the Imam, the Most Noble Master, Muhyi al-Sunnah, the Supporter of Hadith, the Leader of the Imams, the Manifestation of Islam, the Mufti of the East, al-Husayn ibn Masʿud, may Allah have mercy on him."]] It is possible that the revelation preceded the ruling, as in His words, "and you are a dweller in this city";[[Qur'an 90:2.]] the surah is Meccan, yet the effect of this lawful status appeared on the Day of the Conquest, to the point that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Lawfulness was granted to me for an hour of a day."[[Part of a hadith narrated by Muslim in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on the sanctity of Mecca, its game, its trees and its lost property, no. 1354, 2/988; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/300–301.]] Likewise, the following was revealed in Mecca: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs﴾.[[Qur'an 54:45.]] ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "I did not know which multitude would be routed, until on the day of Badr I saw the Prophet ﷺ leaping in his armour and saying: 'The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs.'"[[Mentioned earlier in surah al-Qamar: 7/434.]]

﴿And remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾, i.e., he remembers his Lord and prays. It is said: the remembrance is the *takbirat* of the ʿId, and the prayer is the ʿId prayer. It is also said: the prayer here means supplication.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 87, verses 16–19:

﴿Nay, you prefer the life of this world.﴾ Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub recited [yu'thirun] (they prefer) with the ya' (yā’, the third person masculine), meaning the wretched ones (al-ashqayn) who were mentioned. The others recited it with the ta' (tā’, the second person), and the evidence for this is the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Nay, you (plural) prefer the life of this world." [And what is meant by "the wretched one" (al-ashqa) is the plural, even though it is in the singular form, because when the alif and lam of genus (al-jins) is attached to a noun, it becomes all-encompassing, so it is as if he said: "The wretched ones avoid it." Then he said: "Nay, you prefer the life of this world."]

﴿And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.﴾ 'Arfajah al-Ash'ari said: We were with Ibn Mas'ud when he recited this verse, and he said to us: "Do you know why we preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter?" We said: "No." He said: "Because the world was presented to us, and its food, its drink, its women, its pleasures and its splendour were hastened for us, while the Hereafter was described to us and kept hidden from us, so we loved what is immediate and left what is deferred." [Narrated by al-Tabari, 30/157. The author of al-Durr al-Manthur (8/487) added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (4/502) and said: "This is from him in the manner of humility and self-abasement, or it is a report about the species as such, and Allah knows best."]

﴿Indeed, this﴾ means what was mentioned in His saying: "He has succeeded who purifies himself" [up to the completion of] [Omitted from "b".] four verses, ﴿is in the former scriptures﴾, that is, in the earlier books that were revealed before the Qur'an, in which the success of the one who purifies himself and prays was mentioned, and the preference of people for the life of this world over the Hereafter, and that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

Then he clarified the scriptures, saying: ﴿The scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾. 'Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: this surah is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ma'qil al-Maydani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya [ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Kathir narrated to us] [Omitted from "a".] Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the two rak'ahs before the witr, "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," and "Say: O disbelievers," and in the witr, "Say: He is Allah, the One," and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak," and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind." [Narrated by al-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar (1/285), al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (1/24), and al-Hakim, who declared it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (1/305), and al-Dhahabi agreed; also Ibn Hibban (p. 175 in Mawarid al-Zam'an), al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (2/37), and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (3/99–100). Ibn al-Jawzi criticised it on account of Yahya ibn Ayyub; Abu Hatim said he is not to be used as evidence, and Imam Ahmad and Yahya ibn Ma'in denied the addition of the two mu'awwidhat. Ibn al-Sakan in his Sahih narrated a supporting report from 'Abd Allah ibn Sarjis with a strange isnad. See: Tanqih al-Tahqiq by Ibn 'Abd al-Hadi (2/1060–1061), Talkhis al-Habir (2/18–19).]

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ma'qil al-Maydani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya [ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Kathir narrated to us] [Omitted from "a".] Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the two rak'ahs before the witr, "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High," and "Say: O disbelievers," and in the witr, "Say: He is Allah, the One," and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak," and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind." [Narrated by al-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar (1/285), al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (1/24), and al-Hakim, who declared it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (1/305), and al-Dhahabi agreed; also Ibn Hibban (p. 175 in Mawarid al-Zam'an), al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (2/37), and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (3/99–100). Ibn al-Jawzi criticised it on account of Yahya ibn Ayyub; Abu Hatim said he is not to be used as evidence, and Imam Ahmad and Yahya ibn Ma'in denied the addition of the two mu'awwidhat. Ibn al-Sakan in his Sahih narrated a supporting report from 'Abd Allah ibn Sarjis with a strange isnad. See: Tanqih al-Tahqiq by Ibn 'Abd al-Hadi (2/1060–1061), Talkhis al-Habir (2/18–19).]
